accent: No accent control. Pads are velocity-sensitive with eight levels and three response curves (Soft, Medium, Loud), or sensitivity can be turned off (SOS Jan 1988).

built_in_effects.name: None (no effects processor)
built_in_effects.notes: Vintage Synth Explorer: 'Effects - None'. A few ROM samples carry recorded ambience or gating by name: Ambient Snare ('wood ambient snare' in SOS), 22" Gated Kick, Gated Snare.

global_features: 16 velocity-sensitive pads, 16 voices (one per pad)
49 sounds, 16-bit; claimed 47 kHz sample rate and 20 kHz bandwidth
kit (VOICE/TUNE/MIX including pan) stored per pattern; empty patterns default to the standard voice assignment, no pitch shift, nominal mix
tuning -16 to +15 per pad ('from 12 semitones flat to almost seven semitones sharp' per SOS Nov 1988)
7-position pan; two stereo output pairs; front volume slider controls output 1 only
100 patterns (up to 682 beats each) and 100 songs (up to 255 steps)
quantise 1/4 to 1/64 or off; SWING function (values not documented in the sources found)
OFFSET shifts drum events in 1/384-note steps up to 99/384 (per SOS Jan 1988 review)
MIDI note per pad; MIDI drum receive/transmit off by default
UK price GBP 449 inc VAT (1988)

categories.name: Hi-hats (closed A/B, half open, open, foot closed)

pack_contents: 'Alesis HR-16': 19 WAVs, 16-bit/44.1 kHz, 2-channel but L/R nearly identical (centred mono), named by instrument without numbers: Agogo Bell, Bassdrum, Cabasa, Clap, Claves, Closed Hat, Conga H, Conga L, Maracas, Open Hat, Rim, Shaker, Snaredrum, Timbale, Tom-1, Tom-2, Triangle, Wood Block H, Wood Block L. No ride, crash, mid hat, toms 3-4, cowbells, tambourine, snap or sticks. 'Alesis HR16': 44 mono 16-bit/44.1 kHz WAVs prefixed HR16: Kick01-06, Snare01-07, Rimshot, Sidestick, Tom01-04, Hat_C1, Hat_C2, Hat_M, Hat_O, Hat_P, Ride01-02, Crash, Timbale, HiConga, LoConga, Shaker, Block1-2, Clave, Cabasa, Maracas01-02, Agogo, Cowbell01-02, Triangle, Tamborine (sic), Clap, Snap. Against the 49-sound ROM: 6 of 10 kicks, 4 of 5 toms, Drum Sticks missing, one more snare than the ROM's 6 (unexplained). Pack numbers do not follow ROM numbers. No loops or MIDI.

famous_tracks.title: Streetcleaner (album)
famous_tracks.evidence: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Streetcleaner - says Broadrick and G.C. Green used an Alesis HR-16 for nearly all the album's percussion (secondary; seen via search summary).

famous_tracks.title: Lincoln (album)
famous_tracks.evidence: https://tmbw.net/wiki/Drum_Machine - 'It was heavily used on Lincoln, and to a lesser extent on Flood', citing John Flansburgh's Tumblr.

famous_tracks.title: It's a Big Daddy Thing
famous_tracks.evidence: https://www.visualartsdb.com/artwork/si-nmaahc-ld1-1658220228681-1658220241664-0-alesis-hr-16-drum-machine-used-by-prince-paul - mirror of a Smithsonian NMAAHC object 'Alesis HR-16 drum machine used by Prince Paul'; says its sound 'can clearly be heard' on this record (seen only in search snippets; page returned 403).

famous_tracks.title: Chime
famous_tracks.evidence: https://www.soundonsound.com/techniques/classic-tracks-orbital-chime - Paul Hartnoll: 'after that I added 909 and [Alesis] HR16 drum machines' (the HR16 was borrowed from Phil); which drum parts it played is not stated.

famous_tracks.title: Connected
famous_tracks.evidence: https://mixdownmag.com.au/features/mixdowns-greatest-drum-machines-of-all-time-part-one/ - says the HR-16 is 'Famed for being the drum machine used on Stereo MC's track Connected' (uncited); a band interview says only 'an Alesis drum machine'. Low confidence.

accent: No accent control. Pads have eight velocity levels; MIDI triggering uses all 127. The VELOCITY page offers Soft, Medium, Loud or Fixed 1-8. 'Dynamic articulation' changes timbre on hard hits for many sounds (clearly audible on a few kicks, snares, congas, toms). A hit's volume can be edited per step in step mode.

built_in_effects.name: Reverb/ambience recorded into many ROM samples (no effects processor)
built_in_effects.notes: Music Technology 1991: 'a mixture of dry and reverbed sounds'; 94 of 233 sounds are stereo, many of them the reverbed ones (room/hall/ambient kicks, snares, toms). Dry sounds have none. Vintage Synth Explorer: 'Some samples have reverb & ambience in them'.

global_features: 12 velocity-sensitive pads; 16-voice polyphony with voice stealing
233 16-bit sounds (94 stereo) with dynamic articulation
50 preset + 50 user drum sets (per pad: sound, volume, pan, tuning, ASN mode, output)
50 preset + 50 user patterns, each with Main A, Main B, Fill A, Fill B (400 total), 1-128 beats; 100 user songs
swing 54%, 58% or 62% (or off)
96 ppqn record resolution (Music Technology review)
11 velocity responses: Soft, Medium, Loud, Fixed 1-8
tuning +3 to -4 per pad; 7-position pan; Main and Aux stereo outputs
SoundStacking: merge one pad's part onto another pad to layer sounds
MIDI: global note per pad; NORMAL or MULTI-DRUMSET note map (notes 0-119); program change selects user drum sets; clock in/out
start/stop footswitch; tap tempo via footswitch (Quickstart Rev C); tape and MIDI sysex backup; over 15,000 events of memory
UK price GBP 299 inc VAT (1991)

pack_contents: 'Alesis SR-16': 52 WAVs, 16-bit/44.1 kHz, 2-channel but effectively mono (L/R corr >= 0.998) except Guiro and Hit, in sub-folders Bassdrums (Bassdrum-01..13), Snaredrums (Rim, Snaredrum-01..12), Cymbals (Crash-01..02, Hat Closed-01..03, Hat Open-01..03, Hat Reverse, Ride-01..03), Percussion (Block, Bongo, Clap, Congo, Cowbell, Finger, Guiro, Shaker, Tamb, Timbale, Triangle), Misc (Hit, Metal, Synth Cymbal). 'Alesis SR16': 52 mono 16-bit/44.1 kHz WAVs prefixed SR16: Kick01-13, Snare01-12, Rimshot, Hat_C1-C3, Hat_O1-O4, Ride01-03, Crash01-02, Block, Bongo, Clap, Conga, Cowbell01-02, FSnap, Guiro, Shaker, Spark, Tamborine, Tank, Timbale, Triangle. Both have the same structure (13 kicks, 12 snares + rim, 3 rides, 2 crashes, 7 hats, 14 percussion/misc), a small subset of the 233-sound ROM, similar to the free 53-sound Polynominal pack. Pack numbers are not ROM numbers. No loops or MIDI. For the near-complete ROM, see the 'Alesis SR15' folder.

accent: No accent control. Every note responds to velocity (MIDI velocity, or trigger level through per-input gain and velocity curve). Dynamic Articulation changes timbre and pitch with velocity.

built_in_effects.name: Ambience/reverb recorded into many samples (no effects processor)
built_in_effects.notes: SOS Feb 1996: many sounds are recorded with ambience or reverb, so external processing 'isn't always necessary'. The manual's functions (Voice, Tune, Mix, Output, Drum Set, Ext Trig, Group, MIDI) include no effects.

global_features: drum sound module: no pads, no sequencer (demo sequence only); 12 trigger inputs plus MIDI
21 drum sets (00-20); factory presets restorable from ROM
61 notes per drum set (MIDI 36-96 by default; root note shiftable so the window can sit anywhere from 0-60 to 67-127)
16-voice polyphony shared across the kit, with voice stealing; more DM5s can be chained for polyphony
8 voice families, including Random (a different sample of the same type on each hit)
4 MB of samples; 18-bit DACs at 48 kHz
per note: tune +3.00 to -4.00 semitones in cent steps, volume 00-99, 7-position pan, Main/Aux output, Multi/Single/Group 1/Group 2
trigger settings: gain, velocity curve, crosstalk, decay, noise; footswitch hi-hat mode or kit stepping
Main L/R and Aux L/R outputs plus headphones; MIDI program-change table; sysex save/load
UK price GBP 499 inc VAT (SOS Feb 1996)
pack_contents: 'Alesis DM5': 470 mono 16-bit/44.1 kHz WAVs in one flat folder, numbered by the pack's own scheme (not the DM5 chart): DM5FX01-64 (64), DM5Kick01-95 (95), DM5Snare001-109 (108; 028 missing), DM5Rim01-09 (9), DM5Hat_C01-10 (9; C08 missing), DM5Hat_O01-10 (9; O07 missing), DM5Perc001-114 (114), DM5Tom01-25 as _Hi/_M/_Lo variants (62 files; incomplete sets: Tom03/04/05/16/18/19 Hi+Lo only, Tom07 and Tom09 Hi only, Tom08 Lo+M, Tom10 Lo only; Tom25 uses '_Mid'). No cymbals (Cym family) and no Random family. 'Rim' is not a DM5 family. No loops or MIDI.
